subject: gnomeTinkerer
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: gnome tinkerer with a backpack of gadgets.
Style: whimsical low-poly mix.
reasoning:
I'm planning a gnome tinkerer figure around 0.9 meters tall with a pointy hat, designing a full skeleton with hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, articulated arms and legs, and a backpack, set on a wooden workshop platform with gears.

Still defining the skeleton hierarchy and joint positions...

Now setting up the arms symmetrically for left and right sides, placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist points in an A-pose with arms slightly extended outward and down.

I'm defining the arm chain as a polyline through these three points, parenting it to the chest, then sweeping it with a tapered radius to form sleeve geometry, adding a hand sphere at the wrist with simple chunky fingers and a thumb for gloved hands. For the legs, I'm setting hip, knee, and ankle points symmetrically to build the leg chain down to the foot.

Boots are boxes with a rounded sphere toe sitting flush at ground level, with the leg chain sized short and colored to suggest pants tucked into cuffed boots. For the torso I'm going simpler -- just an ellipsoid sphere scaled and positioned at the spine bone, painting it as a jacket with plain colors, reserving grain and brass paint effects for wood and clockwork details elsewhere.

I'll pull in the clockwork kit for gears, gauges, and coil textures, then set up a small helper function to place parts on bones with consistent options. The jacket gets a custom paint function that mixes warm highlight tones on top and cool shadow tones below based on surface normal, giving the gnome's coat a bit of shading depth without full cel-shading.

Now I'm positioning the head and facial features: a scaled sphere for the head, a bulbous red nose, and decal-based eyes computed from the head's spherical surface geometry so they sit flush on the front.

For the beard, I'm planning layered cone-shaped spikes radiating downward from the chin to form a big white beard, arranging rows of tapered spikes with varying spread to build volume.

Still designing facial features...

Positioning the hat with a tilt, lathing the brim and lower cone up to a certain height, then sweeping a curved, bent tip off to the side for a whimsical look, attaching it all at the head bone.

Now I'm adding a hat band with a thin torus ring, giving the hat a classic brick-red color, and placing a small decorative gear on the front of the band as an accent.

For the goggles, I'm positioning the lens cylinders near the hat band since the brim covers the forehead area, placing brass-rimmed glowing lenses slightly offset to either side and bridging them with the central gear.

Adding a tiny gear between the goggles, then giving the glass lens a cyan glow cylinder offset outward. Checking that the hat brim clears the head and eyes properly since the hat sits low on the head, with the base cone radius fitting within the head's curvature. Now starting on the backpack shape.

I'm checking that the strap points stay just outside the torso ellipsoid surface at each shoulder and belly position, adjusting coordinates slightly where they land too close to or inside the body.

Now I'm thinking through the backpack's gadget details: a brass telescope poking out one side with tapered tube sections, a wrench sticking out with steel coloring, a coiled spring, and a gauge texture on the back face of the pack.

I'm also planning a small gear train mounted on the backpack's back, facing outward, with three interlocking gears of varying teeth counts, spokes, and holes, sized small enough to fit within the pack's width alongside the gauge.

Working out the gear rotation directions around the axis to figure out where gear1 and gear2 land relative to gear0, placing gear1 toward +X and computing gear2's offset at -120 degrees for the layout.

I'm also planning smaller details: adjusting the gauge position, hanging a glowing amber lantern with brass caps off the left side of the pack, sticking a wrench up from the top-left, and routing a steel spring coil down the right side.

I'm adding a telescope swept from the pack angling up and back with banded sections, a darker flap for the pack lid, and a whimsical touch—a small two-blade propeller mounted on a pole at the top. I'm also sketching small tool pouches as boxes and considering a torus-based belt sweep around the waist.

Switching to a simpler circular tube section for the belt instead of an elliptical sweep since the orientation was ambiguous, with a brass buckle box in front and a hammer hanging at the hip made from a capsule handle and box head. Now I'm moving on to the brown leg sweeps and starting the tunic skirt.

For the tunic, I'll lathe a flared profile from the hips down to around y .14, with a gold torus trim ring at the hem. For sleeves, I'm adding cuff torus rings at the wrists oriented along the arm direction from elbow to wrist, then simple sphere hands at the wrist ends, with the right hand set up to hold a wrench.

Fingers I'll keep simple: skip the gripping pose, use open mitt-style hands with a palm and three finger rods plus a thumb, offset slightly along the perpendicular axis and extended along the forearm direction, avoiding extra joint complexity.

Now I'm figuring out the base platform: rather than add a global offset for feet sinking into the base, I'll keep the boot bottoms and base bottom both at y=0, with a thin lathe-turned round wooden platform (~0.025 height, 0.5 radius) so the boots sink minimally and it stays under the 2% height threshold, plus a raised rim and scattered decorations like cogs, mushrooms, a toolbox, and screws.

For the floor props, I'm placing a flat gear lying on the ground at the right thickness offset above the platform, adding a small two-gear meshing pair nearby with static joints under "hips," and arranging a spotted mushroom cap-and-stem and a brass toolbox around the scene, while reconsidering whether to keep or drop the glowing lantern prop.

Now I'm deciding on remaining props and face details: keeping the lantern on the floor, adding a spring/wrench/telescope to the pack, skipping extra mechanical creatures but adding a few hex nut/screw lathe props. For the face, I'm planning a nose sphere, decal eyes and brows, blush decals, and a separate jaw sphere (with the beard attached to a jaw bone so it moves naturally) with its own joint near the chin.

I'm now working out decal textures -- eye SVGs with white sclera and brown pupils, a gear emblem decal for the tunic chest, and a "TINKER" text patch for the pack.

I'm defining the torso part geometry with a scaled sphere positioned on the spine bone to host the chest emblem decal, and considering flat-shaded low-poly spheres for a faceted look elsewhere. Then I'm building the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, spine and chest joints with spine roles, followed by arm chains (shoulder, elbow, wrist) parented to the chest with an "arm" role, and starting on the leg chain next.

Working out the leg joints (hip, knee, ankle) parented to hips with a leg role, then sweeping tapered geometry along both the leg and arm chains for sleeves and pant legs, using the tip joints as the bone references for boots and hands. I'm positioning shoulder, elbow, and wrist points for the arm in a neutral A-pose, computing the hand direction vector from wrist to elbow, and starting to lay out finger offsets for a flat mitten-style hand using perpendicular axes.

I'm defining helper functions for building capsule-shaped limb segments with color and bone parameters, importing shading and texture utilities like mix, paint, grain, mottle, stripes, and noise from the builder SDK, and setting up a shading function that blends highlight and shadow colors based on surface normal direction, plus establishing base color constants like skin tone before moving into hat coloring.

For the hat I'm designing tone-on-tone red stripes rather than contrasting colors, using sine-wave noise to create subtle spiraling bands across the cone shape, then wrapping that pattern through the same lighting function that blends highlights and shadows based on normal direction.

Now I'm fleshing out the full gnome tinkerer build: defining jacket green with mottled noise shading, a leather vest with paneled rivets, a textured beard grain pattern, and then moving into the boot and leg geometry—placing ankle cuffs, toe caps, and sweeping the leg shape from hip to knee.

Checking proportions for the pelvis sphere, tunic skirt lathe, and torso bottom so hemlines align correctly against the knees and thighs, then positioning the head joint and jaw for the beard attachment point.

Now I'm working out the beard's layered structure—a flat sphere base mass plus a series of spike cones arranged by x/y/z coordinates to form individual beard strands tapering to points.

I'm computing where the beard base intersects the head sphere's surface at the jawline, then plotting spike base and tip coordinates so the beard hangs naturally over the chest without clipping into the torso.

Now I'm positioning the mustache with a curved sweep path tucked just under the nose, checking surface clearance against the head sphere so it doesn't poke through, then starting the eye decal placement using similar surface-distance calculations.

Next I'm working out brow capsules angled above the eyes, sizing them against the head's curvature so they sit shaggy but contained, then moving to the hat band torus and hat lathe profile — fitting the torus radius to the hat's flare at that height and sketching the lathe points for the hat's silhouette from brim to crown.

I'm continuing the hat's tip, sweeping it to a point with a small gold bell at the end, then checking that the overall hat height stays within sink limits and that the brim doesn't obscure the eyes from a front view. Then I start setting up the goggles, orienting the lens cylinders along the hat band with tilted axes and sizing the frame rings.

Now I'm placing the hat gear decoration and working out positions so it sits centered between the goggle lenses without overlapping. Then I move to designing the backpack as a box with a separate lid, working out its depth so it sits flush against the torso's back, and placing a gear train on its rear face with proper thickness offsets.

For the pack details, I'm positioning a gauge dial above the gears and sizing a second gear so it doesn't collide with the first, then adding side pockets to hold protruding tools -- a wrench on one side and a telescope on the other. I'm now defining the wrench's outline as a polygon, carefully laying out coordinates for the handle and jaw head so the shape doesn't self-intersect.

Still writing extrusion and placement logic...

Still defining the propeller blades...

Now I'm thinking through where to place a rolled blanket cylinder on top of the pack, but it conflicts with the propeller position, so I'm repositioning the propeller to avoid overlap with the blanket and side pocket items.

For the floor scene, I'm designing a lantern made of brass cylinders, a hexagonal glass lathe shape with an amber glow, a flame sphere inside, and a cone cap, while also placing gears, a mushroom, and a toolbox nearby with careful spacing so none of these floor props overlap.

I'm checking distances for the gear positions relative to the base radius, worried gear teeth might collide with the gnome's boots given certain rotation angles, so I'm adjusting the angle to push the gear train further out toward -X to avoid that overlap while still staying within the base rim.

For the mushroom, I'm sketching a small stem cylinder with a lathe-profiled cap colored red with painted spots, scaled down with a second smaller mushroom nearby, and placing both along with the toolbox and lantern at safe distances from the base edge. I'm also planning a small gold gear-and-wrench decal for the tunic chest and considering a "TINKER" text patch decal on the backpack lid.

I'm checking the hanging hammer placement on the hip belt, working out the rod and head geometry so it clears the skirt's radius profile, and adjusting the belt ellipse dimensions so it sits properly outside the skirt silhouette without clipping.

I'm adding a brass buckle box in front of the belt, then trying to work out an apron plate over the torso's curved front -- figuring out whether it floats or needs resizing to match the belly's curvature at different heights.

The apron idea keeps colliding with the skirt radius though, so I'm abandoning the full apron and instead planning a smaller pocket box or emblem patch fitted onto the skirt surface itself, checking its offset so it protrudes just slightly without overlapping the skirt geometry.

Now I'm shifting to the gear train setup for the chest bone, defining gear modules and spin joints that parent to the chest and naming the gear joints sequentially.

Adding the gauge texture plane and backing ring...

I'm now sketching an eye icon with an SVG, using an ellipse for the eye shape, layered circles for the iris and pupil, with a highlight dot.

Then I'm designing a gear-shaped emblem using a dashed-stroke circle for teeth plus a solid ring and crossing wrench line, and placing it as a decal on the torso near the chest.

But the beard covers that area, so I need to reposition — maybe shrink the beard so its tips sit higher, placing the emblem lower at the torso/skirt boundary where it stays visible.

Settling on a shorter beard with tip around y.50 and side tips higher, putting the emblem at y.43 sized small enough to clear the belt line below it. Now I'm defining the helper function for building parts with geometry, color, bone, and position, and starting to lay out the sphere and other primitives for the figure.

I'm setting up color constants for metals (brass, gilt, steel, copper, blued) and importing the glow effect, then writing the sleeve geometry using a tapered sweep along the arm chain. Now I'm working out the hand and finger placement math, positioning the palm as an offset sphere from the wrist joint and spacing three fingers outward from it.

Positioning the thumb inward and forward relative to the palm, then building each fingertip as a capsule extending along the arm direction, checking that the hand ends up at a reasonable height above the floor. Finally I'm adding a cuff as a torus oriented along the arm direction near the wrist.

Now I'm adding details like a cream rolled cuff, a small brown elbow patch, and a shoulder ball joint linking to the first arm bone, then planning to write out the module with bone hierarchy and metadata export. I'm also sketching in white sideburn spikes under the hat and considering a gilt hat bell sphere, plus whether to use a color property directly in the lathe geometry options for the spotted material.

Writing paint functions...

Placing ear base and tip positions, then adding a nose sphere and small cheek accents on the head surface.

I'm also adding a hidden jaw sphere tucked behind the beard, then finalizing by returning the root bone — keeping the code simple with plain number arrays for points rather than complex types.

Writing skeleton code...
